title: Tomato Early Blight (Alternaria solani)
content: Tomato Early Blight caused by Alternaria solani produces distinct concentric dark brown to black rings ('target-like' lesions) on older leaves. Surrounding tissue yellowing occurs early. Leaves gradually drop starting from bottom of plant. Warm, moist weather (75–85°F) promotes spore germination.
immediate_actions: Prune affected lower leaves that touch or are near the soil.
Avoid overhead irrigation to keep leaves dry.
Ensure adequate row spacing to improve canopy airflow.
prevention: Practice 3-4 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Apply organic straw mulch around plant base to prevent soil splash.
Plant resistant or tolerant tomato varieties.
ipm: Monitor lower leaves weekly for early target spots.
Use bio-fungicides like Bacillus subtilis at first sign of infection.
Remove and destroy crop debris immediately after harvest.
verified_treatments: Copper octanoate (copper soap) bio-approved fungicide application per label instructions.
Potassium bicarbonate foliar spray for early surface inhibition.
safety_precautions: Always wear gloves and protective eye wear when applying copper fungicides.
Do not apply copper sprays during extreme heat (>90°F / 32°C) to prevent leaf burn.
Observe 1-day Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) for bio-copper preparations.

title: Tomato Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans)
content: Tomato Late Blight is a devastating water mold pathogen caused by Phytophthora infestans. Symptoms include large, dark water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems, often with white cottony fungal growth on the underside during cool humid weather. Plants can collapse rapidly within days.
immediate_actions: Immediately destroy heavily infected plants by bagging and discarding (do not compost).
Isolate surrounding plants and cease sprinkler irrigation.
Notify neighboring growers as spores travel long distances in wind.
prevention: Use certified disease-free transplants.
Eliminate volunteer tomato and potato plants near fields.
Choose well-drained fields with high sun exposure.
ipm: Track regional weather advisories for late blight spore warnings.
Apply protective preventive bio-copper before extended humid, cool periods.
biological_controls: Bacillus amyloliquefaciens strain D747 preventive bio-fungicide.
verified_treatments: Preventive fixed copper hydroxide or copper sulfate treatments under certified label conditions.
Mancozeb or Chlorothalonil protectant sprays where locally registered and approved.
safety_precautions: Check localized agricultural extension bulletins for approved active ingredients.
Observe strict Pre-Harvest Intervals (PHI 5-7 days depending on formulation).
Wear full protective clothing (N95 mask, nitrile gloves, chemical splash goggles).

title: Potato Early Blight (Alternaria solani)
content: Alternaria solani affects potato foliage and tubers. Leaves exhibit dark brown, target-ring lesions bounded by leaf veins. Severe infections cause premature defoliation and tuber size reduction.
immediate_actions: Maintain proper field nitrogen levels; nitrogen-deficient plants are highly susceptible.
Avoid leaf wetness duration over 8 hours.
prevention: Crop rotation with corn, beans, or small grains.
Destroy potato vine residue post-harvest.
ipm: Foliar bio-fungicide protection during early flowering.
Regular scouting of lower canopy leaves.
verified_treatments: Chlorothalonil or Azoxystrobin applications per agricultural extension guidelines.
safety_precautions: Follow product label application limits to prevent fungicide resistance build-up.

title: Corn Common Rust (Puccinia sorghi)
content: Puccinia sorghi produces small, powdery cinnamon-brown pustules on both upper and lower corn leaf surfaces. As leaves mature, pustules turn dark brown to black. Favored by high humidity and moderate temperatures (60-77°F).
immediate_actions: Assess crop growth stage; rust late in grain filling rarely causes economic loss.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant corn hybrids.
Early planting to avoid peak airborne spore concentrations.
ipm: Scout upper leaves around tasseling stage (VT to R1).
Apply fungicides only if susceptible hybrids exceed threshold (10-15% leaf area affected).
biological_controls: Bio-control options limited; focus on host plant resistance.
verified_treatments: Strobilurin or Triazole class fungicides where threshold exceeded.
safety_precautions: Respect label Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) for silage or grain harvest.

title: Rice Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae)
content: Magnaporthe oryzae causes diamond-shaped or spindle-shaped lesions with gray/white centers and reddish-brown borders on leaves. Collar blast and neck rot can lead to complete panicle loss.
immediate_actions: Maintain deep water level in paddies to suppress spore germination.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties certified by local agriculture authority.
Treat seeds with bio-fungicide before sowing.
ipm: Balanced fertilizer management (split N doses, adequate Potassium and Silicon).
biological_controls: Pseudomonas fluorescens seed treatment and foliar spray.
verified_treatments: Tricyclazole or Isoprothiolane where registered and strictly regulated.
safety_precautions: Prevent water runoff into aquatic habitats when using agricultural treatments.

title: Apple Scab (Venturia inaequalis)
content: Apple Scab produces olive-green to dark brown velvety spots on leaf surfaces and fruit. Infected fruit becomes deformed, cracked, and premature drop occurs.
immediate_actions: Rake and destroy fallen overwintered leaf litter under trees.
prevention: Plant scab-resistant cultivars (e.g., Liberty, Enterprise, Freedom).
Prune canopy annually to promote rapid drying.
ipm: Use Mills Table infection models to time sprays post-rain events.
biological_controls: Sulfur or Lime Sulfur organic sprays.
verified_treatments: Liquid Lime-Sulfur application during green tip to pink bud stage.
Captan or Myclobutanil under guided spray calendars.
safety_precautions: Do not apply sulfur within 14 days of oil applications.

title: Grape Powdery Mildew (Erysiphe necator)
content: Erysiphe necator appears as white to ash-gray powdery coating on leaves, green shoots, and berries. Causes berry scarring, splitting, and off-flavors in wine/table grapes.
immediate_actions: Improve fruit-zone leaf pulling to increase sun exposure and wind passage.
prevention: Maintain open canopy architecture with hedging and shoot positioning.
ipm: Early season preventive sulfur applications start at 2-3 inch shoot growth.
safety_precautions: Avoid sulfur applications when temperatures exceed 90°F (32°C) to prevent leaf damage.

title: Wheat Stripe Rust (Puccinia striiformis)
content: Wheat Stripe Rust produces bright yellow-orange pustules arranged in linear stripes along leaf veins. Rapid leaf chlorosis and premature leaf death occur in cool, wet spring weather (45-60°F).
immediate_actions: Scout flag leaves carefully at boot stage.
prevention: Plant stripe rust-resistant wheat varieties (e.g. Yr gene resistance).
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization.
ipm: Apply foliar bio-protection at early stem elongation.
biological_controls: Bacillus amyloliquefaciens seed and foliar bio-protection.
verified_treatments: Tebuconazole or Propiconazole foliar fungicide application per regional threshold.
safety_precautions: Observe 30-day Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) for grain harvest.

title: Cotton Bacterial Blight (Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum)
content: Bacterial Blight of cotton produces angular, dark brown to black water-soaked lesions bounded by leaf veinlets (Angular Leaf Spot). Systemic infection causes black arm stem lesions and boll rot.
immediate_actions: Avoid field cultivator entry when leaves are wet to reduce mechanical transmission.
prevention: Use acid-delinted, certified disease-free planting seed.
Grow bl-gene resistant cotton cultivars.
ipm: Incorporate cotton crop residues deeply immediately after picking.
biological_controls: Copper hydroxide + Bacillus bio-formulation preventive sprays.
verified_treatments: Fixed copper bactericides applied preventively early in canopy growth.
safety_precautions: Do not mix copper products with strongly acidic foliar fertilizers.

title: Pepper Bacterial Spot (Xanthomonas euvesicatoria)
content: Bacterial Spot affects leaves and fruit of pepper. Leaves develop small, water-soaked, dark green spots that turn dark brown with raised margins. Severe infections cause extensive defoliation.
immediate_actions: Switch from overhead sprinkler to drip line irrigation immediately.
prevention: Plant bacterial spot resistant bell pepper varieties (Bs1, Bs2 genes).
Treat seeds with hot water or sodium hypochlorite.
ipm: Sanitize field stakes and trays with 10% bleach solution between seasons.
verified_treatments: Copper hydroxide combined with Mancozeb for improved bacterial control.
safety_precautions: Always wear nitrile gloves and splash goggles when handling copper bactericides.

title: Strawberry Leaf Scorch (Diplocarpon earlianum)
content: Diplocarpon earlianum causes dark purple spots on strawberry leaves. Unlike leaf spot, scorch spots broaden into irregular purple blotches without white centers, giving foliage a sun-scorched appearance.
immediate_actions: Mow and collect old foliage immediately after harvest renovation.
prevention: Plant in full sun with straw mulch bed elevation.
Select leaf scorch tolerant strawberry cultivars.
ipm: Ensure proper plant spacing (12-18 inches) to maximize air movement.
verified_treatments: Fixed copper octanoate or Captan preventive sprays during bloom.
safety_precautions: Respect 1-day Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) for fresh market strawberry harvest.
